rankings.summaryHtml: The Hawks are up to 22-2 since their 7-6 start and have climbed from 26th overall in defensive efficiency to No. 5. Hollinger's strength of schedule table says Atlanta has had an easier ride than all but four teams ... but a league-leading 13 wins over .500-or-better teams tells a different tale.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Dubs must be wondering what they have to do to reclaim No. 1. rankings.summaryHtml: Question: Do we dock Portland points because a league-high 21 of its 30 wins have been recorded against sub-.500 teams? Answer: Can't dock too many when the Blazers are 21-2 against losing teams and Golden State is 19-1. Especially when you factor in the Blazers' injuries along the front line.

rankings.summaryHtml: This is the first time in a long time -- going all the way back, in fact, to 2009-10 -- that the Spurs will lose more than 15 games before the All-Star break. Their 23 wins in 38 games is actually tied for the lowest win total through 38 games in the Tim Duncan era, matching a 23-15 start in 2000-01.

rankings.summaryHtml: Only seven players have ever managed a PER of 30-plus in a single season. Anthony Davis, at a robust 31.12, is on track to become just the fourth all time at 6-foot-10 or taller, joining Shaq, David Robinson and Wilt. He'd also be the youngest at 21; T-Mac topped the 30 mark when he was 23 in 2002-03.
